headline: Every major above its 200-day, RSI screaming hot, and whales still moving coin to exchanges
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it is unusually clean today: six of seven majors sit above their 200-day trend line, only ADA sits below it (down 76.9% from its 12-month high, the laggard of the group). BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB and DOGE all show MACD above signal too, so trend and momentum are pointing the same direction across almost the entire board. That kind of agreement is rare and worth naming plainly: this is a market where the dominant assets are all in uptrend, not a mixed tape where you have to pick your spots.

But look at the momentum gauges and the picture gets more interesting. SOL is printing an RSI-14 of 85.4, BTC sits at 82.1, BNB at 81, ETH at 78. These are not merely overbought readings, they are the kind of numbers that show up when a rally has been running hot for a while without pausing to digest. BTC is up 24.5% on the week and 24.1% on the month, SOL up 41.2% on the week, XRP up 45.7% on the week. Trend and momentum agree on direction, but momentum is stretched far enough that it deserves flagging on its own: an RSI in the 80s is not a divergence from trend, it is trend running at a pace that historically does not hold without some kind of rest.

Positioning tells a calmer story than the price action does. BTC funding on OKX sits at 0.0021% per 8 hours, annualized to just 2.3%, and ETH funding is similarly mild at 3.4% annualized. Funding is the fee longs pay shorts (or vice versa) to hold a leveraged position open; low positive funding here means traders are not paying up aggressively to stay long, despite prices near their 90-day highs. That is not what a crowded, over-leveraged rally usually looks like. The liquidation data leans the same way: over the last 17 hours, BTC shorts lost $10.9 million to $1.8 million for longs, and ETH shorts lost $15.9 million versus $8.4 million for longs. Shorts are the ones getting run over, not longs, which fits a market grinding higher without excess long leverage stacked on top.

Flows are where the tension actually lives. ETF money keeps arriving: BTC spot ETFs took in $232.2 million on 26 Aug, extending an 8-day streak of same-direction flow with $1.80 billion net over the last five sessions; ETH ETFs added $192.4 million on the same day, also 8 days running, $891.3 million over five sessions. That is real traditional-finance demand showing up daily. At the same time, whale wallets moved a net $301.3 million onto exchanges over the last 48 hours, with BTC contributing $131.0 million net onto exchanges and ETH $170.2 million net onto exchanges, both flagged toward Coinbase institutional. Zoom out to the weekly view and the onto-exchange pattern is not a one-off: the last three weeks (Aug 13, Aug 20, and the week ending Aug 27) all show net flow onto exchanges, a reversal from the $1.06 billion that moved off exchanges in the week ending Aug 06. Coin moving toward exchanges while ETFs buy and prices grind up is not a contradiction that resolves itself in the data, it is simply two different flows pointing different ways at once.

Sentiment sits at 71, Greed, inside its own 30-day range of 25 to 74, so the crowd is nearly as euphoric as it has been all month. Stablecoin float is essentially flat, up just 0.76% over 30 days to $309.2 billion, meaning the dry powder on the sidelines has not meaningfully grown even as prices ran. What to watch from here: whether the onto-exchange whale pattern extends into a fourth straight week, whether BTC and ETH funding starts climbing meaningfully above today's low single digits as leverage builds into strength, and whether the ETF streak (currently 8 days same-direction for both BTC and ETH) breaks. Any one of those flipping would be the first real crack in a tape that, for now, is uniformly bullish on trend and uniformly hot on momentum.
